reconcile.note: John Gill reads Moses' words about no longer going out and coming in as resignation of office, not bodily decline, consistent with the vigor reported at his death.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells reads Moses' admission that he can no longer go out and come in as a plain acknowledgment of infirmity that contradicts his undimmed eye and unabated strength.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: I am one hundred twenty years old this day; I can no more go out and come in: and Yahweh has said to me, You shall not go over this Jordan.
sides.verseText: He said to them, I am one hundred twenty years old this day; I can no more go out and come in: and Yahweh has said to me, You shall not go over this Jordan.

sides.snippet: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
sides.verseText: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
